findings.description: The reports bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No ACL is set and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block for this bucket, so bucket/object ACLs or policies could grant public read/write access to archived reports.
The bucket has no logging block, so access to sensitive report data cannot be audited or attributed after a compromise.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects overwritten or deleted by an attacker (or by terraform destroy) are unrecoverable.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial export data unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured for the ledger bucket, so reads and writes of sensitive ledger exports go unrecorded.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so ledger objects can be silently overwritten or permanently deleted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose ledger data publicly.
The model artifacts bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so ML artifacts (which may embed proprietary or personal data) are stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving it vulnerable to accidental public exposure via ACL or policy.
The runbooks bucket lacks server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks frequently contain hostnames, procedures, and credentials and are stored unencrypted.
No logging block is defined, so access to operational runbooks is not audited.
There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricting public ACLs or policies on the runbooks bucket.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The audit/log-delivery bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or reading of the centralized audit logs is not itself recorded.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket allows all audit records to be deleted along with the bucket, undermining log integrity and non-repudiation.
The audit bucket uses the permissive 'log-delivery-write' canned ACL and has no public access block, so log data access controls rely entirely on ACLs that could be widened.
The vendor roster object is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument into a bucket that has no default encryption, so potentially sensitive vendor data is stored in plaintext.
